text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Smart-routing abnormality detected. High churn in route health between us-east-1, us-west-2, and eu-west-1. 60s window shows >1200 reroutes. Pager sent to #incidents and @mike (oncall).

mike (oncall): I got the page, looking now. Any customer impact?

sara (eng-sre): Seeing 502/504 spikes for a subset of traffic hitting the fallback cluster. Some customers in us-east report higher latency, others in eu time out. Not full outage but clear error spike correlated with route flips.

lee (runtime): Logs show repeated health-check deregistration then re-registration for same backend id across regions. Looks like: backend-uuid X moves us-east -> fails -> routed to us-west -> health-check succeeds -> then us-east sees it healthy again and flips back. Repeat.

alara (prodops): That sounds like a probe ‘flip-flop’ rather than true host crash. Can we pin the health-check trace?

ops-bot: Health-check sample (most recent):
```
{
  "probe_id": "hc-7f2b",
  "target": "model-serving-pool-3",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "status": "500",
  "response_time_ms": 120,
  "variant": "v2-int8",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-15T18:24:12Z"
}
```

lee (runtime): Interesting: probe response contains variant=v2-int8 but the fallback policy in the routing control plane is configured to compare variant affinity TTL using a different naming convention (we recently changed variant naming to include build-id). The control plane's comparator is returning mismatch and marking instances unhealthy transiently.

mike (oncall): So the routing policy is treating healthy nodes as unhealthy due to string mismatch -> causes rapid rerouting? Can we confirm exact config?

sara (eng-sre): Pulling current policy: 
```
$ curl -sS https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/routing/policies/default | jq .
{
  "name": "smart-region-fallback",
  "order": ["prefer-latency","prefer-variant-affinity"],
  "variant_match": "^v\d+-[a-z]+$",
  "variant_ttl_s": 60
}
```

lee (runtime): There it is. Our variant names now look like v2-int8-b1234 but the regex expects no suffix. So variant_match fails -> comparator treats it as a different variant every time the build-id rotates or tags appear. That toggles affinity state and TTL expiry causes de-registration bounce.

alara (prodops): That explains the hopstorm between regions. If affinity TTL is 60s and comparator fails, the system thinks affinity changed often and keeps moving clients.

mike (oncall): Mitigation plan? Can we patch the control plane rule to relax matching or temporarily disable prefer-variant-affinity?

lee (runtime): Quick mitigation options: 
1) Update variant_match to a looser regex to accept the new suffixes (safe, low-risk).
2) Increase variant_ttl_s to 300 to reduce churn (temporary).
3) Disable the prefer-variant-affinity step entirely (more impact on latency/cost).

mike (oncall): Do 1) immediately, 2) if we still see churn, then 2). Don't disable entirely without PM/eng approval.

ops-bot: Applying config patch to control-plane (dry-run then apply).

ops-bot: Dry-run output: 
```
PATCH /api/v1/routing/policies/default
payload: { "variant_match": "^v\d+-[a-z]+(-b\d+)?$" }
result: dry-run OK
```

ops-bot: Applying patch...

ops-bot: Patch applied. New policy: variant_match: ^v\d+-[a-z]+(-b\d+)?$

sara (eng-sre): Monitoring metrics -> reroute_count falling from 20/s to ~2/s in the last 45s. Error spikes dropping.

lee (runtime): Confirmed: health-check de/registrations reduced dramatically. The probe still occasionally returns 5xx for single checks but no sustained oscillation.

mike (oncall): Good. Can we also add a temporary metric alert to detect variant name mismatches so we catch this earlier?

alara (prodops): I'll file an action item: add a control-plane validation that rejects regexs that don't match current variant samples and add a canary test in deploy pipelines. Ticket CREATED: P-3421.

mike (oncall): Customer impact summary: transient increased 500/504 for ~12 min window, small subset of customers in us-east and eu experienced degraded responses. No data loss. Postmortem required.

ops-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring.

lee (runtime): Root cause: variant naming convention change (build-id suffix) + brittle variant_match regex in routing policy + short variant_ttl leading to churn.

sara (eng-sre): Follow-ups: 1) Add regex auto-sample validation in control plane (P-3421), 2) Add end-to-end canary for routing policy changes (P-3422), 3) Increase default variant_ttl to 180s as safety (P-3423).

mike (oncall): I'll run the incident timeline and assign owners. Thanks team. If anything flares back up ping me directly. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: Incident recorded. Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC.

mike (oncall): Closing thread for now, leaving monitoring in place.

ops-bot: Last check at 2026-03-15T18:28:30Z -> reroute_rate: 1.8/s, error_rate down 85% compared to peak.
